text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said the 29 billion crown deficit in trade with Russia would not be reduced by lowering Slovak imports. The problem must be solved by increasing Slovak exports, said Meciar.
- Meciar said the government would reconsider Moscow's proposal to create a free-trade zone because it could help the trade balance with Russia.
- Slovak Privatisation Minister Peter Bisak said it was not yet possible to capitalise through privatisation Russian debts to Slovakia.

- Opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) said it did not expect any significant changes to privatisation bodies, parliamentary committees supervising the Slovak secret service (SIS) nor the official television STV to take place at the forthcoming session of parliament.
PRAVDA - Oil refiner Slovnaft said it might be considering another increase of prices of its petrol fuels if the current upward trend in world oil prices continues.
- Meciar said the state could extend only about two billion crowns out of the needed initial capital of 10 billion for a planned export-import bank.

SME - The Constitutional Court has ruled that the foreign ministry violated the constitutional right for free entry to the country of Michal Kovac Junior, son of the Slovak President, when it did not react after Kovac Junior's abduction to Austria in September last year.
- Leading Slovak actors from major theatres have repeatedly called for resignation of the minister of culture Ivan Hudec.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - State subsidies to agriculture totalled 10.3 billion crowns over last two years.
